chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

It is recommended that a fresh palm stalk be placed with him in his grave, that his grave be raised above the ground by the measure of four joined fingers, that water be sprinkled upon it, and that he be left alone.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِ أَصَابِعَ مَضْمُومَةٍ: the measure of four joined fingers, indicating the recommended grave height
key_terms.جَرِيدَةٌ رَطْبَةٌ: a fresh palm stalk placed with the deceased in the grave
key_terms.قَبْرِهِ: his grave, the place of burial
key_terms.يُخَلَّى عَنْهُ: he is left alone after burial
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: it is recommended as a non-obligatory legal ruling
key_terms.يُنْضَحَ: water is sprinkled lightly over the grave

ai.seo_question: What burial practices are recommended for the deceased in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states recommended rites connected to burial: placing a fresh palm stalk in the grave, raising the grave slightly, sprinkling water over it, and then leaving the deceased. It reflects juridical guidance on the etiquette and recommended practices of burial in Shia tradition.
